name: Google Earth Pro
description: Google Earth Pro was a desktop app that gave users access to Google Earth with more advanced features.

name: Firebase Studio
description: Firebase Studio is an agentic, cloud-based development environment that gives you powerful tools and AI agents directly in your browser.

name: Office Online Server
description: Office Online Server was an on-premise version of browser-based Office applications hosted on companies proprietary clouds rather than Microsoft's.

name: Microsoft Publisher
description: Microsoft Publisher was a desktop publishing application focusing on page layout and graphic design rather than text composition and proofreading.

name: Teams Live Chat
description: Teams Live Chat was a website chat widget that allowed businesses to connect with website visitors and route incoming conversations directly into Microsoft Teams.

name: GitHub Classroom
description: GitHub Classroom was a free tool designed to help educators using GitHub distribute coding assignments, provide automated feedback, and manage coursework using GitHub repositories.

name: Microsoft Whiteboard
description: Microsoft Whiteboard was a free multi-platform application, as well as an online service and a feature in Microsoft Teams, which simulates a virtual whiteboard and enables real-time collaboration between users.

name: Tenor API
description: Tenor API was used for searching up and sharing GIFs in Tenor's database on other websites (notably Discord).

name: 3D Viewer
description: 3D Viewer (formerly Mixed Reality Viewer and before that, View 3D) was a 3D computer graphics viewer and augmented reality application that was first included in Windows 10 1703.

name: Pixel Studio
description: Pixel Studio allowed users to quickly generate AI images using a prompt and provided a library of past generative images.

name: Doppl
description: Doppl was an early experimental AI app launched by Google Labs in June 2025 to create a "digital twin" or virtual model of yourself for trying on outfits.

name: .NET Interactive
description: .NET Interactive was an engine and an API that allows to run, test, and edit code interactively, often combined with notebook technologies such as Jupyter.

name: Polyglot Notebooks
description: Polyglot Notebooks was an extension which brought support for multi-language (Jupyter) notebooks to Visual Studio Code.

name: Azure Data Studio
description: Azure Data Studio was a data management and development tool with connectivity to popular cloud and on-premises databases.

name: Dark Web Reports
description: Dark Web Reports was a dark web scanner that searched for personal info leaks.

name: Microsoft Lens
description: Microsoft Lens (formerly Microsoft Office Lens) was a OneNote companion app designed to capture, scan and enhance images of whiteboards and printed documents and store them in various formats.

name: Steam for Chromebooks
description: Steam for Chromebooks is an beta initiative that allowed users to install and run PC games via the Steam client.

name: Mac Pro
description: Apple's tower workstation line for professionals who needed maximum expansion and maximum invoices. After years of shrinking relevance beside Mac Studio, Apple finally discontinued the line entirely.

name: Viva Goals
description: Viva Goals was a goal-setting and management solution that uses the OKR (Objectives and Key Results) framework, derived from the acquisition of Ally.io.

name: Tables by A120
description: Tables was a collaborative database platform and competitor to Airtable, focused on making project tracking more efficient with automation.

name: Skype for Business
description: Skype for Business (formerly Microsoft Lync and Office Communicator) was an enterprise instant messaging software developed by Microsoft as part of the Microsoft Office suite.

name: Outlook Lite
description: Outlook Lite was a smaller, lighter version of Outlook Mobile, having multi-account, calendar, and SMS support in a relatively tiny footprint and no Copilot.

name: Microsoft Movies & TV
description: Microsoft Movies & TV (previously Xbox Video and Zune Video) was a digital video service developed that offered movies and TV shows available for rental or purchase as well as an app where users can watch videos from their locally-stored digital collections.

name: Microsoft Math Solver
description: Microsoft Math Solver (formerly Microsoft Mathematics and Microsoft Math) was an entry-level educational app that solved math and science problems. Until 2015, it was an app for Windows, then it was released as a service.

name: Bing Maps for Enterprise
description: Bing Maps for Enterprise (previously Microsoft Virtual Earth) was a geospatial mapping platform allowing developers to create applications that layer location-relevant data on top of licensed map imagery.

name: Remote Desktop
description: Remote Desktop was an app to access remote Windows PCs for Windows, macOS, Android, and iOS.

name: Windows Bridge for iOS
description: Windows Bridge for iOS (a.k.a. WinObjC) was an open-source project allowing reuse of existing apps and libraries written in Objective-C to create Universal Windows Platform (UWP) apps that would run on many Windows devices.

name: Skype
description: Skype was a proprietary telecommunications application operated by Skype Technologies, a division of Microsoft, best known for IP-based videotelephony, videoconferencing and voice calls.

name: Dev Home
description: Dev Home was a control center for Windows providing the ability to monitor projects in your dashboard using customizable widgets, set up your dev environment by downloading packages, connect to your developer accounts, and accomplishing many other typical tasks for a developer.

name: Visual Studio App Center
description: Visual Studio App Center was a set of integrated services for building, testing, releasing, and monitoring mobile and desktop apps.

name: Windows Subsystem for Android
description: Windows Subsystem for Android was a feature of Windows 11 which allows users to install and run Android apps.

name: iPhone SE (3rd gen)
description: Apple's last iPhone with a Home button, Touch ID, an LCD screen, and a Lightning port. Discontinued when Apple replaced the SE line with the iPhone 16e.

name: Clips
description: Apple's playful short-form video editor for iPhone and iPad, with captions, filters, stickers, posters, and effects. It outlived several social-video trends before Apple finally stopped updates and downloads.

name: Launchpad
description: MacOS’s app launcher, showing installed apps in an iPad-like grid so a user could open, organize, search, and delete apps quickly. It was replaced in MacOS Tahoe by Spotlight Applications folder

name: Mail
description: Mail was an email client developed by Microsoft and was included in the OS since Windows Vista until Windows 11.

name: Calendar
description: Calendar was a personal calendar application made by Microsoft included in its OS since Windows Vista to Windows 11, offering synchronization among calendar services of different providers.

name: Delve
description: Delve is used to manage users' Microsoft 365 profile, and to discover and organize via machine learning the information that's likely to be most interesting to them across Microsoft 365.

name: Surface Studio
description: Surface Studio was an all-in-one PC famous for featuring a unique hinge design that allows it be tilted to a flat position.

name: TakeLessons
description: TakeLessons was a platform for freelance teachers to connect with students.

name: Paint 3D
description: Paint 3D was a raster graphics and 3D computer graphics application which should have been the successor of Microsoft Paint.

name: Flip
description: Flip (formerly Flipgrid and originally Vidku) was a free-to-use video discussion platform bought by Microsoft for use in classroom environments.

name: Surface Duo
description: Surface Duo was a family of foldable dual-screen smartphones based on Android.

name: Google Jamboard
description: Google Jamboard was a web app, native whiteboard app, and standalone whiteboard hardware that offered a collaborative experience.

name: Windows Mixed Reality
description: Windows Mixed Reality was a platform which provides augmented reality and virtual reality experiences with compatible head-mounted displays.

name: WordPad
description: WordPad was a word processor more advanced than the Notepad text editor by supporting rich text editing, but with a subset of the functionality of Microsoft Word.

name: Socratic
description: Socratic was a free educational app that helped students with homework by scanning questions with a smartphone camera and offering step-by-step solutions.

name: Visual Studio for Mac
description: Visual Studio for Mac was an integrated development environment (IDE) and, despite the name, it was a rebranded version of MonoDevelop that reused some components of the main Visual Studio.

name: Chromecast
description: Chromecast was a line of digital media players that allowed users to play online content on a television.

name: Xbox Games Store
description: Xbox Games Store (formerly Xbox Live Marketplace) was a digital store for Xbox 360 games.

name: Azure Media Services
description: Azure Media Services was a media streaming service that enabled customers to encode, store, and stream video and audio at scale.

name: VPN by Google One
description: VPN by Google One was a virtual private network service that provided users encrypted transit of their data and network activity and allowed them to mask their IP address.

name: Xamarin
description: Xamarin was the first native cross-platform mobile application development framework which provided the basis for MAUI framework.

name: Microsoft Stream (classic)
description: Microsoft Stream (classic) was a corporate video-sharing service that replaced the former Office 365 Video; notably, it included free storage of hosted videos.

name: DropCam
description: Dropcam was a line of Wi-Fi video streaming cameras acquired by Google in 2014.

name: Google Podcasts
description: Google Podcasts was a podcast hosting platform and an Android podcast listening app.

name: Keen
description: Keen was a Pinterest-style platform with ML recommendations.

name: Google Cache
description: Google Cache was a tool to view cached/older versions of a website. It was one of the oldest products.

name: Yammer
description: Yammer was an internal communication system for the genealogy website Geni.com launched in 2008 and then acquired by Microsoft in 2012.

name: Windows Server Essentials
description: Windows Server Essentials (formerly Small Business Server or SBS) was an integrated server suite for businesses with no more than 25 users or 50 devices.

name: Hyper-V Server
description: Hyper-V Server was a free limited version of Windows Server with Hyper-V role to support an enterprise-class virtualization, finally superseded by Azure services.

name: Wiki for MS Teams and Sharepoint
description: Wiki for MS Teams and Sharepoint was a simple and effective Wikipedia embedded in these two products.

name: Apple Pay Later
description: Apple's own buy-now-pay-later service, letting users split purchases into four payments. Barely a year after launch, Apple abandoned the in-house version and shifted toward third-party installment providers.

name: Apple USB SuperDrive
description: The external CD and DVD drive that survived long after Apple removed optical drives from Macs. After 16 years, it quietly went out of stock worldwide and effectively disappeared.

name: Cortana
description: Cortana was a virtual assistant that uses the Bing search engine to perform tasks such as setting reminders and answering questions for the user.

name: Azure Kinect
description: Azure Kinect was a PC peripheral which employs the use of artificial intelligence sensors for computer vision and speech models, and it was connected to the Azure cloud.

name: Google Domains
description: Google Domains was a domain name registrar operated by Google.

name: Google Optimize
description: Google Optimize was a web analytics and testing tool that allowed users to run experiments aimed at increasing visitor conversion rates and overall satisfaction.

name: Glass Enterprise Edition
description: Glass Enterprise Edition was a head-up display for enterprise customers.

name: Microsoft Kaizala
description: Microsoft Kaizala was a secure messaging and work management software application for collaboration among users inside and outside of organizations, including the ability to send and receive instant messages, coordinate tasks, and submit invoices.

name: Soundscape
description: Soundscape was a service for iOS that aims to give people who are blind or visually impaired a greater awareness of their surrounding by using 3D cues.

name: Pixel Pass
description: Pixel Pass was a program that allowed users to pay a monthly charge for their Pixel phone and upgrade immediately after two years.

name: Google Cloud IoT Core
description: Google Cloud IoT Core was a managed service designed to let customers securely connect, manage, and ingest data from globally dispersed devices.

name: Google Album Archive
description: Google Album Archive was a platform that allowed users to access and manage their archived photos and videos from various Google services, such as Hangouts and Picasa Web Albums.

name: YouTube Stories
description: YouTube Stories (originally YouTube Reels) allowed creators to post temporary videos that would expire after seven days.

name: Grasshopper
description: Grasshopper was a free mobile and web app for aspiring programmers that taught introductory JavaScript and coding fundamentals using fun, bite-sized puzzles.

name: Conversational Actions
description: Conversational Actions extended the functionality of Google Assistant by allowing 3rd party developers to create custom experiences, or conversations, for users of Google Assistant.

name: Jacquard
description: Jacquard was a small tag to make it easier and more intuitive for people to interact with technology in their everyday lives, without having to constantly pull out their devices or touch screens.

name: Google Currents (2019)
description: Google Currents was a service that provided social media features similar to Google+ for Google Workspace customers.

name: Google Street View (standalone app)
description: Google Street View app was an Android and iOS app that enabled people to get a 360 degree view of locations around the world.

name: AltspaceVR
description: AltspaceVR was a vibrant, community-centric, VR platform (acquired in 2017), which hosted events including comedy shows, festivals, and weddings.

name: Google Code Competitions
description: Google Code Jam, Kick Start, and Hash Code were competitive programming competitions open to programmers around the world.

name: Google Stadia
description: Google Stadia was a cloud gaming service combining a WiFi gaming controller and allowed users to stream gameplay through web browsers, TV, mobile apps, and Chromecast.

name: Google OnHub
description: Google OnHub was a series of residential wireless routers manufactured by Asus and TP-Link that were powered by Google software, managed by Google apps, and offered enhanced special features like Google Assistant.

name: Touch Bar
description: The OLED strip that replaced the function key row on MacBook Pros. A programmable, context-sensitive control surface that most users ignored, most developers never supported, and Apple finally dropped with the last 13-inch MacBook Pro.

name: Lightning Connector
description: Apple's slim, reversible 8-pin connector, used on iPhone for more than a decade. Replaced on new iPhones by USB-C in 2023 after years of regulatory and industry pressure.

name: iPhone 13 mini
description: The last genuinely small modern iPhone, beloved by a vocal minority and ignored by enough buyers that Apple killed the mini line in 2023.

name: Photo Stream
description: Apple's free photo sync service that automatically pushed the last 1,000 photos to all your Apple devices for 30 days. Replaced by iCloud Photos and finally shut down in 2023 after running quietly in the background for 12 years.

name: Apple Music Voice Plan
description: A cheaper Siri-only Apple Music subscription that removed the normal app interface from streaming. Apple killed it after less than two years, presumably because yelling song requests at Siri was not the future.

name: iMovie Theater
description: iMovie's iCloud-backed showcase for shared clips, movies, and trailers across Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV. Apple eventually dropped support and told users to move everything into iCloud Photos instead.

name: Dark Sky
description: The beloved hyperlocal weather app famous for minute-by-minute rain alerts. Apple acquired it, shut down the Android app and API, then folded its best ideas into Apple Weather.

name: MagSafe Battery Pack
description: Apple's magnetic battery pack for iPhone 12 and later, elegant but small and slow compared with third-party alternatives. Discontinued when the iPhone moved from Lightning to USB-C.

name: MagSafe Duo Charger
description: Apple's folding travel charger for iPhone and Apple Watch. Clever, overpriced, and discontinued alongside the MagSafe Battery Pack after the USB-C iPhone transition.

name: YouTube Originals
description: YouTube Originals was a variety of original content including scripted series, educational videos, and music and celebrity programming.

name: Threadit
description: Threadit was a tool for recording and sharing short videos.

name: Atom
description: Atom was a free, hackable, cross-platform and open-source text editor developed by GitHub with support for plug-ins written in JavaScript and embedded Git Control.

name: Duplex on the Web
description: Duplex on the Web was a Google Assistant technology that automated tasks on the web on behalf of a user; such as booking movie tickets or making restaurant reservations.

name: Google Hangouts
description: Google Hangouts was a cross-platform instant messaging service.

name: Google Surveys
description: Google Surveys was a business product by Google aimed at facilitating customized market research.

name: YouTube for Wii
description: YouTube for Nintendo Wii was an app that let Wii and Wii U users stream YouTube videos on their TVs.

name: YouTube Go
description: YouTube Go was an app aimed at making YouTube easier to access on mobile devices in emerging markets through special features like downloading video on wifi for viewing later.

name: Google My Business (app)
description: Google My Business was an app that allowed businesses to manage their Google Maps Business profiles.

name: Google Chrome Apps
description: Google Chrome Apps were hosted or packaged web applications that ran on the Google Chrome browser.

name: Kormo Jobs
description: Kormo Jobs was an app that allowed users in primarily India, Indonesia, and Bangladesh to help them find jobs nearby that match their skills and interests.

name: Android Auto for phone screens
description: Android Auto for phone screens was an app that allowed the screen of the phone to be used as an Android Auto interface while driving, intended for vehicles that did not have a compatible screen built in.

name: Internet Explorer
description: Internet Explorer (formerly Microsoft Internet Explorer and Windows Internet Explorer, commonly abbreviated IE or MSIE) was the default web browser of Windows OS before the launch of Edge.

name: Google Duo
description: Google Duo was a video calling app that allowed people to call someone from their contact list.

name: G Suite (Legacy Free Edition)
description: G Suite (Legacy Free Edition) was a free tier offering some of the services included in Google's productivity suite.

name: Google Assistant Snapshot
description: Google Assistant Snapshot was the successor to Google Now that provided predictive cards with information and daily updates in the Google app for Android and iOS.

name: Forza Street
description: Forza Street (previously Miami Street) was a free-to-play racing game dow Windows 10, Android, and iOS.

name: Cameos on Google
description: Cameos on Google allowed celebrities and other public figures to record video responses to the most common questions asked about them which would be shown to users in Google Search results.

name: Windows Storage Server
description: Windows Storage Server was a variant of the Windows Server operating system targeted towards network-attached data storage solutions.

name: Android Things
description: Android Things was an Android-based embedded operating system (originally named Brillo) aimed to run on Internet of Things (IoT) devices.

name: Groove Music
description: Groove Music was an audio player software application that was included with Windows 8 to Windows 11, inheriting the main features from Xbox Music and Zune Marketplace.

name: iPod touch
description: The last surviving iPod, an iPhone without the cellular contract. Beloved by kids, travelers, and budget-conscious music fans for 15 years. The end of an era.

name: macOS Server
description: Apple's server OS, once a serious enterprise product with directory services, file sharing, and device management. Wound down over years until it became just a few GUI wrappers.

name: Apple SIM
description: A carrier-switching SIM system for cellular iPads, designed to make mobile data plans less tied to one network. Eventually made redundant by eSIM, and new activations ended in 2022.

name: 27-inch iMac
description: The big-screen iMac that defined desktop Macs for over a decade. Apple killed it after launching Mac Studio and Studio Display, leaving the 24-inch iMac as the only all-in-one Mac.

name: AngularJS
description: AngularJS was a JavaScript open-source front-end web framework based on MVC pattern using a dependency injection technique.

name: Streams
description: Streams was a "clinician support app" which aimed to improve clinical decision-making and patient safety across hospitals in the United Kingdom.

name: Microsoft Academic
description: Microsoft Academic was a free public web search engine for academic publications and literature.

name: Material Gallery
description: Material Gallery was a collaboration tool for UI designers, optimized for Google's Material Design, with mobile preview apps and a Sketch plugin.

name: Google Toolbar
description: Google Toolbar was a web browser toolbar that provided a search box in web browsers like Internet Explorer and Firefox.

name: Channel 9
description: Channel 9 was a website for hosting videos and podcasts that Microsoft employees create.

name: Google Sites (Classic)
description: Google Sites (Classic) allowed users to build and edit websites and wiki portals for private and public use.

name: Your News Update
description: Your News Update was a service that offered an audio digest of a mix of short news stories chosen at that moment based on a user's interests, location, user history, and preferences, as well as the top news stories out there.

name: Google My Maps
description: My Maps was an Android application that enabled users to create custom maps for personal use or sharing on their mobile device.

name: Silverlight
description: Microsoft Silverlight (or simply Silverlight) was an application framework for writing and running rich Internet applications, similar to Adobe Flash.

name: Backup and Sync
description: Backup and Sync was a desktop software tool for Windows and macOS that allowed users to sync files from Google Drive to their local machine.

name: Google Bookmarks
description: Google Bookmarks was a private web-based bookmarking service not integrated with any other Google services.

name: Chatbase
description: Analytics platform for Google's Dialogflow chatbot & others, started by the Google-funded Area120 incubator then retired and partially merged into Dialogflow itself.

name: VR180 Creator
description: VR180 Creator allowed users to edit video taken on 180-degree and 360-degree devices on multiple operating systems.

name: Posts on Google
description: Posts on Google allowed notable individuals with knowledge graph panels to author specific content that would appear in Google Search results.

name: Fitbit Coach
description: Fitbit Coach (formerly Fitstar) was a video-based bodyweight workout app that used AI to personalize workouts based on user feedback.

name: Fitstar Yoga
description: Fitstar Yoga was a video-based yoga app that created unique yoga sessions based on user preference and skill level.

name: Tour Builder
description: Tour Builder allowed users to create and share interactive tours inside Google Earth with photos and videos of locations.

name: Expeditions
description: Expeditions was a program for providing virtual reality experiences to school classrooms through Google Cardboard viewers, allowing educators to take their students on virtual field trips.

name: Tour Creator
description: Tour Creator allowed users to build immersive, 360° guided tours that could be viewed with VR devices.

name: Poly
description: Poly was a distribution platform for creators to share 3D objects.

name: Minecraft Earth
description: Minecraft Earth was a Augmented Reality mobile game that allowed its players to collect blocks and build creations.

name: Google Play Movies & TV
description: Google Play Movies & TV, originally Google TV, was an app used to view purchased and rented media and was ultimately replaced with YouTube.

name: Measure
description: Measure allowed users to take measurements of everyday objects with their device's camera utilizing ARCore technology.

name: Zync Render
description: Zync render was a cloud render platform for animation and visual effects.

name: Timely
description: Timely Alarm Clock was an Android application providing an alarm, stopwatch, and timer functionality with synchronization across devices.

name: Gears Pop!
description: Gears Pop! was a mobile real-time strategy video game in which two players battle using Funko Pop!-stylized characters from the Gears of War fictional universe.

name: Polymer
description: Polymer was an open-source JS library for web components

name: Flight Arcade
description: Flight Arcade was a web-app clone of Flight Simulator game created as a showcase of Microsoft Edge support for modern HTML5 and JavaScript.

name: Google Shopping Mobile App
description: The Google Shopping Mobile App, which had absorbed Google Express when it launched, provided a native shopping experience with a personalized homepage for mobile users. It is now retired and the functionality lives on in the Shopping Tab.

name: Google Public Alerts
description: Google Public Alerts was an online notification service owned by Google.org that sends safety alerts to various countries.

name: Google Go Links
description: (also known as Google Short Links) was a URL shortening service. It also supported custom domain for customers of Google Workspace (formerly G Suite (formerly Google Apps)).

name: Google Crisis Map
description: Google Crisis Map was a website that allowed to create, publish, and share maps by combining layers from anywhere on the web.

name: Cortana (for Mobile)
description: Cortana (for Mobile) was the frontend app for iOS and Android to access to the virtual assistant Cortana.

name: Google Cardboard
description: Google Cardboard was a low-cost, virtual reality (VR) platform named after its folded cardboard viewer into which a smartphone was inserted.

name: Swift for TensorFlow
description: Swift for TensorFlow (S4TF) was a next-generation platform for machine learning with a focus on differentiable programming.

name: Microsoft Image Composite Editor
description: Image Composite Editor was an advanced panoramic image stitcher made by the Microsoft Research division.

name: People
description: People was a contact management app and address book included in Windows 8 and 10.

name: Tilt Brush
description: Tilt Brush was a room-scale 3D-painting virtual-reality application available from Google, originally developed by Skillman & Hackett.

name: Loon
description: Loon was a service to provide internet access via an array of high-altitude balloons hovering in the Earth's stratosphere

name: App Maker
description: App Maker was a tool that allowed its users to build and deploy custom business apps easily and securely on the web without writing much code.

name: Apple Remote
description: Apple's minimalist infrared remote for Macs, iPod docks, and early Apple TVs, first in white plastic and later in aluminum. It faded out as Siri Remote and software remotes took over.

name: iTunes U
description: Platform for universities, schools, and educators to share lectures and course materials through iTunes. Quietly shut down and partially absorbed into Apple Podcasts.

name: HomePod (1st gen)
description: Apple's premium smart speaker with genuinely excellent audio quality. Discontinued in 2021 as Apple focused on the cheaper HomePod mini, before reviving the full-size HomePod in 2023.

name: iMac Pro
description: The Space Gray all-in-one workstation Apple built as a stopgap for professionals waiting on a real Mac Pro. Expensive, powerful, barely updated, and eventually replaced in spirit by Mac Studio.

name: Google Cloud Print
description: Google Cloud Print allowed users to 'print from anywhere;' to print from web, desktop, or mobile to any Google Cloud Print-connected printer.

name: Google Home Max
description: Google Home Max was a large, stereo smart speaker with two tweeters and subwoofers, aux input, and a USB-C input (for wired ethernet) featuring Smart Sound machine learning technology.

name: Science Journal
description: Science Journal was a mobile app that helped you run science experiments with your smartphone using the device's onboard sensors.

name: YouTube VR (SteamVR)
description: YouTube VR allowed you to easily find and watch 360 videos and virtual reality content with SteamVR-compatible headsets.

name: Trusted Contacts
description: Trusted Contacts was an app that allowed users to share their location and view the location of specific users.

name: Windows 10 IoT Core
description: Windows 10 IoT Core was an embedded OS for smaller and lower-cost industry devices, it was also provided free of charge for use in devices like the Raspberry Pi for hobbyist use.

name: Windows Application Driver
description: Windows Application Driver (WinAppDriver) was an open-source service to support Selenium-like UI Test Automation on Windows Applications.

name: Google Play Music
description: Google Play Music was a music and podcast streaming service, and online music locker.

name: Nest Secure
description: Nest Secure was a security system with an alarm, keypad, and motion sensor with an embedded microphone.

name: YouTube Community Contributions
description: YouTube Community Contributions allowed users to contribute translations for video titles or submit descriptions, closed captions or subtitles on YouTube content.

name: Hire by Google
description: Google Hire was an applicant tracking system to help small to medium businesses distribute jobs, identify and attract candidates, build strong relationships with candidates, and efficiently manage the interview process.

name: Password Checkup extension
description: Password Checkup provided a warning to users if they were using a username and password combination checked against over 4 billion credentials that Google knew to be unsafe.

name: Playground AR
description: Playground AR (aka AR Stickers) allowed users to place virtual characters and objects in augmented reality via the Camera App on Pixel phones.

name: Focals by North
description: Focals were a custom-built smart glasses product with a transparent, holographic display that allowed users to read and respond to text messages, navigate turn-by-turn directions, check the weather, and integrate with third-party services like Uber and Amazon Alexa.

name: Cortana (for Xbox)
description: Cortana (for Xbox) was the frontend app to access to the virtual assistant Cortana.

name: CallJoy
description: CallJoy was an Area 120 project that provided phone automation for small-to-medium businesses allowing them to train the bot agent with responses to common customer questions.

name: Mixer
description: Mixer was a video game live streaming platform, originally named Beam before the acquisition by Microsoft.

name: Google Photos Print
description: Google Photos Print was a subscription service that automatically selected the best ten photos from the last thirty days which were mailed to user's homes.

name: Pigeon Transit
description: Pigeon Transit was a transit app that used crowdsourced information about delays, crowded trains, escalator outages, live entertainment, dirty or unsafe conditions.

name: EdgeHTML
description: EdgeHTML was a proprietary browser engine used in Microsoft Edge and in Universal Windows Platform (UWP) apps.

name: Enhanced 404 Pages
description: Enhanced 404 Pages was a JavaScript library that added suggested URLs and a search box to a website's 404 Not Found page.

name: Shoelace
description: Shoelace was an app used to find group activities with others who share your interests.

name: Neighbourly
description: Neighbourly was a mobile app designed to help you learn about your neighborhood by asking other residents, and find out about local services and facilities in your area from people who live around you.

name: Wunderlist
description: Wunderlist was a cloud-based task management application, acquired by Microsoft in June 1, 2015.

name: Fabric
description: Fabric was a platform that helped mobile teams build better apps, understand their users, and grow their business.

name: Google Contributor
description: Google Contributor was a program run by Google that allowed users in the Google Network of content sites to view the websites without any advertisements that are administered, sorted, and maintained by Google.

name: Material Theme Editor
description: Material Theme Editor was a plugin for Sketch App which allowed you to create a material-based design system for your app.

name: Google Station
description: Google Station was a service that gave partners an easy set of tools to roll out Wi-Fi hotspots in public places. Google Station provided software and guidance on hardware to turn fiber connections into fast, reliable, and safe Wi-Fi zones.

name: One Today
description: One Today was an app that allowed users to donate $1 to different organizations and discover how their donation would be used.

name: Androidify
description: Androidify allowed users to create a custom Android avatar for themselves and others.

name: Google Fiber TV
description: Google Fiber TV was an IPTV service that was bundled with Google Fiber.

name: Microsoft Internet Games
description: Microsoft Internet Games was a bundle of online games bundled in Windows Me, XP, and 7.

name: Remix 3D
description: Remix 3D was a website for users to browse, distribute, and download 3D objects.

name: Apple TV Remote app
description: Apple's official iPhone and iPad app for controlling Apple TV. Pulled from the App Store after Apple moved the remote into Control Center.

name: Network Utility
description: A Mac app for network diagnostics: ping, traceroute, port scanning, Whois lookups. A staple for sysadmins and power users, deprecated in macOS Big Sur.

name: Smart Battery Case
description: Apple's official iPhone case with a built-in battery, instantly recognizable for the hunchback bulge that broke every other iPhone case design rule. Quietly discontinued in 2020 once MagSafe wireless charging arrived.

name: iBooks Author
description: Apple's Mac app for creating interactive ebooks and textbooks. It once looked like the future of digital publishing, then Apple folded its core features into Pages and pulled the app for new users.

name: Field Trip
description: Field Trip was a mobile app that acted as a virtual tour guide by cross-referencing multiple sources of information to provide users information about points of interest near them.

name: AdSense (mobile app)
description: AdSense (mobile app) allowed users to manage their AdSense accounts in a native app for iOS and Android.

name: Windows Phone
description: Windows Phone was a family of mobile operating systems for smartphones as the replacement successor to Windows Mobile and Zune.

name: Google Correlate
description: Google Correlate was a service that provided users information about how strongly the frequency of multiple search terms correlates with each other over a specified time interval.

name: Google Translator Toolkit
description: Google Translator Toolkit was a web application which allowed translators to edit and manage translations generated by Google Translate.

name: Google Fusion Tables
description: Google Fusion Tables was a web service for data management that provided a means for visualizing data in different charts, maps, and graphs.

name: Google Bulletin
description: Google Bulletin was a hyperlocal news service where users could post news from their neighborhood and allow others in the same areas to hear those stories.

name: HealthVault
description: HealthVault was a web-based personal health record to store and maintain health and fitness information.

name: HealthVault Connection Center
description: HealthVault Connection Center was a client-side tool to allow users to upload data from personal health devices to the HealthVault service.

name: Touring Bird
description: Touring Bird was an Area 120 incubator project which helped users compare prices, book tours, tickets, and experiences, and learn about top destinations around the world.

name: HockeyApp
description: HockeyApp was a mobile beta distribution and crash analytics startup acquired by Microsoft in 2014, until the service got integrated into Visual Studio App Center.

name: Game Builder
description: Game Builder was a multiplayer 3D game environment for creating new games without coding experience.

name: Datally
description: Datally (formerly Triangle) was a smart app by Google that helped you save, manage, and share your mobile data.

name: Google Clips
description: Google Clips was a miniature clip-on camera that could automatically capture interesting or relevant video clips determined by machine learning algorithms.

name: Google Daydream
description: Google Daydream was a virtual reality platform and set of hardware devices that worked with certain Android phones.

name: YouTube Leanback
description: YouTube Leanback was an optimized version of YouTube used for television web browsers and WebView application wrappers.

name: Message Center
description: Message Center was a web console where Gmail users could view and manage spam email messages.

name: Follow Your World
description: Follow Your World allowed users to register points of interest on Google Maps and receive email updates whenever the imagery was updated.

name: G Suite Training
description: G Suite Training (previously known as Synergyse) provided interactive and video-based training for 20 Google G Suite products in nine languages through a website and a Chrome extension.

name: YouTube Messages
description: YouTube Messages was a direct messaging feature that allowed users to share and discuss videos one-on-one and in groups on YouTube.

name: YouTube for Nintendo 3DS
description: YouTube for Nintendo 3DS allowed users to stream YouTube videos on the portable gaming console.

name: Office Remote
description: Office Remote was an app to control Office products such as PowerPoint, Word and Excel from an Android or a Windows Phone.

name: Works with Nest API
description: Works with Nest was an API that allowed external services to access and control Nest devices. This enabled the devices to be used with third-party home automation platforms and devices.

name: Google Trips
description: Google Trips was a mobile app that allowed users to plan for upcoming travel by facilitating flight, hotel, car, and restaurant reservations from user's email alongside summarized info about the user's destination.

name: Hangouts on Air
description: Hangouts on Air allowed users to host a multi-user video call while recording and streaming the call on YouTube.

name: Personal Blocklist
description: Personal Blocklist was a Chrome Web Extension by Google that allowed users to block certain websites from appearing in Google search results.

name: Dragonfly
description: Dragonfly was a search engine designed to be compatible with China's state censorship provisions.

name: Google Jump
description: Google Jump was a cloud-based VR media solution that enabled 3D-360 media production by integrating customized capture solutions with best-in-class automated stitching.

name: TouchDevelop
description: TouchDevelop was an educational, touch-friendly and cross-platform app for teaching coding to kids.

name: Blog Compass
description: Blog Compass was a blog management tool that integrated with WordPress and Blogger available only in India.

name: Areo
description: Areo was a mobile app that allowed users in Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, Gurgaon, and Pune to order meals from nearby restaurants or schedule appointments with local service professionals, including electricians, painters, cleaners, plumbers, and more.

name: Microsoft Band
description: Microsoft Band was a line of smart bands with smartwatch and activity tracker/fitness tracker features.

name: YouTube Gaming
description: YouTube Gaming was a video gaming-oriented service and app for videos and live streaming.

name: Google Cloud Messaging (GCM)
description: Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) was a notification service that enabled developers to send messages between servers and client apps running on Android or Chrome.

name: Data Saver Extension for Chrome
description: Data Saver was an extension for Chrome that routed web pages through Google servers to compress and reduce the user's bandwidth.

name: Inbox by Gmail
description: Inbox by Gmail aimed to improve email through several key features.

name: Google+
description: Google+ was an Internet-based social network.

name: Google URL Shortener
description: Google URL Shortener, also known as goo.gl, was a URL shortening service.

name: Google Spotlight Stories
description: Google Spotlight Stories was an app and content studio project which created immersive stories for mobile and VR.

name: Google Allo
description: Google Allo was an instant messaging mobile app for Android, iOS, and Web with special features like a virtual assistant and encrypted mode.

name: Google Notification Widget (Mr. Jingles)
description: Mr. Jingles (aka Google Notification Widget) displayed alerts and notifications from across multiple Google services.

name: Zo
description: Zo was an English chatbot for the principal social networks and messaging apps, born from the experience gained from previous chatbots such as Tay and Xiaoice.

name: Virtual Academy
description: Virtual Academy was a free online training area for Microsoft technologies, replaced by Microsoft Learn.

name: YouTube Video Annotations
description: YouTube Video Annotations allowed video creators to add interactive commentary to their videos containing background information, branching ("choose your own adventure" style) stories, or links to any YouTube video, channel, or search results page.

name: Google Realtime API
description: Google Realtime API provided ways to synchronize resources between devices. It operated on files stored on Google Drive.

name: Chromecast Audio
description: Chromecast Audio was a device that allowed users to stream audio from any device to any speaker with an audio input.

name: Home Team
description: Home Team was a social app for Windows Phone that helps people find the best local service providers by sharing recommendations with friends and coworkers.

name: iTunes
description: The app that defined the digital music era, powered the iPod revolution, and built the App Store. After 18 years of bloat, replaced by Music, Podcasts, and TV apps in macOS Catalina.

name: MacBook (12-inch)
description: Apple's thinnest, lightest laptop, with a single USB-C port, fanless design, and a beautiful Retina display. Too compromised for most buyers; too underpowered to justify its price.

name: 32-bit macOS App Support
description: macOS Catalina dropped 32-bit app support entirely, breaking thousands of games and legacy applications after one major release of prominent warnings.

name: Texture
description: A magazine subscription service born as Next Issue and later rebranded Texture, dubbed "the Netflix of magazines." Apple acquired it in 2018 and folded the idea into Apple News+.

name: 3D Touch
description: Pressure-sensitive display tech enabling Peek, Pop, and shortcut menus based on press force. Quietly dropped from the iPhone XR in 2018, abandoned entirely with the iPhone 11.

name: Mac Pro (Trash Can)
description: The radical cylindrical Mac Pro: striking to look at, thermally compromised inside. Apple went six years without an update and publicly admitted they had "painted themselves into a corner."

name: Dashboard
description: macOS's dedicated layer of mini-apps called widgets, accessed with a keystroke. Groundbreaking in Tiger, disabled by default years later, and finally removed in macOS Catalina.

name: AirPower
description: Apple's wireless charging mat, announced in 2017 to charge iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch at once from almost any position. Canceled in 2019 after Apple said it could not meet its own standards.

name: Back to My Mac
description: A remote access feature that used iCloud to find and connect to your Macs over the internet. Magical when it worked, mysterious when it didn't, and gone from all macOS versions in 2019.

name: Find My Friends
description: Apple's standalone location-sharing app for keeping track of friends and family. Merged into the unified Find My app in iOS 13, alongside Find My iPhone.

name: Google Search Appliance
description: Google Search Appliance was a rack-mounted device that provided document indexing functionality.

name: Google Nearby Notifications
description: Google Nearby Notifications were a proximity marketing tool using Bluetooth beacons and location-based data to serve content relevant to an Android user's real-world location.

name: Google Pinyin IME
description: Google Pinyin IME was an input method that allowed users on multiple operating systems to input characters from pinyin, the romanization of Standard Mandarin Chinese.

name: Google News & Weather
description: Google News & Weather was a news aggregator application available on the Android and iOS operating systems.

name: Reply
description: Reply was a mobile app that let users insert Smart Replies (pre-defined replies) into conversations on messaging apps.

name: Windows MultiPoint Server
description: Windows MultiPoint Server was an operating system based on Microsoft Windows Server using Remote Desktop Services technology to host multiple simultaneous independent computing stations or terminals connected to a single computer (multiseat computing).

name: TruePlay
description: TruePlay was an anti-cheat feature of Windows 10 to add an extra level of protection for videogames.

name: Minecraft: Apple TV Edition
description: Minecraft: Apple TV Edition was the version of Bedrock Edition designed to run on tvOS.

name: Tez
description: Tez was a mobile payments service by Google, targeted at users in India. It was rebranded to Google Pay.

name: Google Goggles
description: Google Goggles was used for searches based on pictures taken by handheld devices.

name: Save to Google Chrome Extension
description: Save to Google Chrome Extension enabled you to quickly save a page link with image and tags to a Pocket-like app.

name: Windows Sets
description: Windows Sets was supposed to be a feature of Windows that allowed all of your apps to be forced into tabs, so you could have different apps next to each other in the same window.

name: Google Play Newsstand
description: Google Play Newsstand was a news aggregator and digital newsstand service.

name: Encrypted Search
description: Encrypted Search provided users with anonymous internet searching.

name: Google Cloud Prediction API
description: Google Cloud Prediction API was a PaaS for machine learning (ML) functionality to help developers build ML models to create application features such as recommendation systems, spam detection, and purchase prediction.

name: Office Excel Viewer
description: Microsoft Excel Viewer was a freeware program for viewing and printing spreadsheet documents created by Excel.

name: Office PowerPoint Viewer
description: PowerPoint Viewer was a free application to be used on computers without PowerPoint installed, to view, project, or print (but not create or edit) presentations.

name: qpx-express-API
description: A service that Google developed for long-tail travel clients. ITA Software will create a new, easier way for users to find better flight information online, which should encourage more users to make their flight purchases online.

name: Google Site Search
description: Google's Site Search was a service that enabled any website to add a custom search field powered by Google.

name: reCAPTCHA Mailhide
description: reCAPTCHA Mailhide allowed users to mask their email address behind a captcha to prevent robots from scraping the email and sending spam.

name: Microsoft Classroom
description: Microsoft Classroom was an online learning platform for schools that aimed to simplify grading assignments and student communication in a paperless way.

name: SoundStage
description: SoundStage was a virtual reality music sandbox built specifically for room-scale VR.

name: AirPort Express
description: Apple's compact Wi-Fi router that doubled as a wired AirPlay audio receiver, beloved by people who wanted wireless audio without replacing their speakers. Gone with the rest of the AirPort line.

name: AirPort Extreme
description: Apple's flagship home Wi-Fi router, later redesigned into a striking vertical tower. Discontinued as Apple exited the router business entirely.

name: Time Capsule
description: A Wi-Fi router with a built-in hard drive for automatic, wireless Time Machine backups. An elegant hardware solution to an everyday problem, killed alongside the AirPort line.

name: iPhone X
description: Apple's tenth-anniversary iPhone, the first with Face ID and an edge-to-edge OLED display. Discontinued exactly one year after launch, an unusually short lifespan for a flagship iPhone.

name: Groove Music Pass
description: Groove Music Pass (formerly Xbox Music Pass and, before, Zune Music Pass) was a music subscription service, which allows subscribers to download an unlimited number of songs for as long as their subscription is active.

name: Project Tango
description: Project Tango was an API for augmented reality apps that was killed and replaced by ARCore.

name: Office Word Viewer
description: Microsoft Word Viewer was a freeware program for Microsoft Windows to display and print Microsoft Word documents.

name: Google Portfolios
description: Portfolios was a feature available in Google Finance to track personal financial securities.

name: Microsoft Kinect
description: Kinect was a line of motion sensing input devices for Windows and Xbox consoles.

name: Lumia
description: Microsoft Lumia (previously the Nokia Lumia Series) was a line of mobile devices that was originally designed and marketed by Nokia and later by Microsoft Mobile.

name: CodePlex
description: CodePlex was a hosting platform for open-source software, offering features such as support to different VCS systems, wiki pages, statistics, and releases.

name: YouTube Video Editor
description: YouTube Video Editor was a web-based tool for editing, merging, and adding special effects to video content.

name: Trendalyzer
description: Trendalyzer was a data trend viewing platform.

name: Stand-alone phones for Skype
description: Skype landline phones, cordless DECT phones, and analog telephone adapters (ATA) were phones to use skype network and account without the need of a PC or a smartphone.

name: Xbox Fitness
description: Xbox Fitness was an online service that took the world’s best fitness videos and made them interactive with the power of Xbox One.

name: Glass OS
description: Glass OS (Google XE) was a version of Google's Android operating system designed for Google Glass.

name: Google Map Maker
description: Google Map Maker was a mapping and map editing service where users were able to draw features directly onto a map.

name: So.cl
description: So.cl (pronounced "social") was a social networking service and social search engine operated by Microsoft FUSE Labs.

name: Chromebook Pixel
description: Chromebook Pixel was a first-of-its-kind laptop built by Google that ran Chrome OS, a Linux kernel-based operating system.

name: Google Spaces
description: Google Spaces was an app for group discussions and messaging.

name: Google Hands Free
description: Google Hands Free was a mobile payment system that allowed users to pay their bill using Bluetooth to connect to payment terminals by saying 'I'll pay with Google.'

name: Microsoft PhotoSynth
description: Microsoft PhotoSynth was a program that generates a three-dimensional model and a point cloud from 2D photos.

name: Build with Chrome
description: Build with Chrome was a collaboration between Chrome and the LEGO Group that allowed users to build and publish LEGO creations to any digital plot of land in the world through Google Maps.

name: Windows Movie Maker
description: Windows Movie Maker (later rebranded as Windows Live Movie Maker) was a video editing software program for home users.

name: Microsoft Essentials
description: Windows Essentials (formerly Windows Live Essentials and Windows Live Installer) is a discontinued suite of freeware applications that includes email, instant messaging, photo sharing, blogging, and parental control software and it was part of Live brand.

name: Visual Studio LightSwitch
description: Visual Studio LightSwitch was an extension and framework specifically tailored for creating line-of-business applications built on existing .NET technologies.

name: Windows Photo Gallery
description: Windows Photo Gallery (formerly known as Windows Live Photo Gallery) was an image organizer, photo editor and photo sharing program and it was part of Windows Essentials software suite.

name: Windows Live Mail
description: Windows Live Mail (formerly named Windows Live Mail Desktop) was a freeware email client designed (but not limited) to use the proprietary DeltaSync protocol and it was the successor to Windows Mail in Windows Vista, which, in turn, was the successor to Outlook Express in Windows XP/98.

name: Gesture Search
description: Google Gesture Search allowed users to search contacts, applications, settings, music, and bookmark on their Android device by drawing letters or numbers onto the screen.

name: 32-bit iOS App Support
description: iOS 11 dropped support for 32-bit apps, rendering thousands of older games and apps permanently unplayable on updated devices. Many developers had already moved on; many users had not.

name: iPod nano
description: The ultra-thin, colorful iPod that evolved through seven generations and countless designs. A design icon of the 2000s and 2010s, killed alongside its sibling with no ceremony.

name: iPod shuffle
description: The tiny clip-on music player with no screen, just shuffle. Simple, cheap, and genuinely fun. The only music player you could wear like a badge.

name: iTunes Festival
description: Apple's annual month-long free concert series at London's Roundhouse, featuring artists from Adele to Pharrell streamed live to iTunes users. Renamed Apple Music Festival in 2015 and quietly ended after the 2016 season.

name: Panoramio
description: Panoramio was a geo-location tagging and photo sharing product.

name: Google Showtimes
description: Google Showtimes was a standalone movie search result page.

name: Pixate
description: Pixate was a platform for creating sophisticated animations and interactions, and refining your designs through 100% native prototypes for iOS and Android.

name: Microsoft WebMatrix
description: Microsoft WebMatrix was a cloud-connected website builder and HTML editor for Windows, geared towards web development.

name: Google Nexus
description: Google Nexus was Google's line of flagship Android phones, tablets, and accessories.

name: Together
description: Together was a watch face for Android Wear that let two users link their watches together to share small visual messages.

name: Sunrise Calendar
description: Sunrise Calendar was a calendar application for web, mobile and desktop, featuring live aggregation of calendars from multiple sources.

name: Project Ara
description: Project Ara was a modular smartphone project under development by Google.

name: Web Hosting in Google Drive
description: Web hosting in Google Drive allowed users to publish live websites by uploading HTML, CSS, and other files.

name: Windows Journal
description: Windows Journal was an application to create and organize handwritten notes and drawing, included in Windows XP Tablet PC Edition as well as select editions of Windows Vista and later.

name: Microsoft SharePoint Designer
description: Microsoft SharePoint Designer (SPD), formerly known as Microsoft Office SharePoint Designer, was an HTML editor freeware for creating or modifying Microsoft SharePoint sites, workflows and web pages.

name: Google Swiffy
description: Google Swiffy was a web-based tool that converted SWF files to HTML5.

name: Google Wallet Card
description: Google Wallet Card was a prepaid debit card that let users pay for things in person and online using their Wallet balance at any retailer that accepted MasterCard.

name: Nexus Player
description: Nexus Player was a digital media player that allowed users to play music, watch video originating from Internet services or a local network, and play games.

name: Revolv
description: Revolv was a monitoring and control system that allowed users to control their connected devices from a single hub.

name: Microsoft InfoPath
description: Microsoft InfoPath was an application for designing, distributing, filling and submitting electronic forms containing structured data.

name: Freebase
description: Freebase was a large collaborative knowledge base consisting of structured data composed mainly by its community members, developed by Metaweb(acquired by Google).

name: Google Now
description: Google Now was a feature of Google Search that offered predictive cards with information and daily updates in Chrome and the Google app for Android and iOS.

name: MyTracks
description: MyTracks was a GPS tracking application for Android which allowed users to track their path, speed, distance, and elevation.

name: uWeave
description: uWeave (pronounced “micro weave”) was an implementation of the Weave protocol intended for use on microcontroller-based devices.

name: Tay
description: Tay was a chatbot that was shutdown after only 16 hours since it began to post inflammatory and offensive tweets through its Twitter account.

name: Google Compare
description: Google Compare allowed consumers to compare several offers ranging from insurance, mortgage, and credit cards.

name: Google Maps Coordinate
description: Google Maps Coordinate was a service for managing mobile workforces with the help of mobile apps and a web-based dashboard.

name: Pie
description: Pie was a work-centric group chat website and app comparable to Slack.

name: Google Maps Engine
description: Google Maps Engine was an online tool for map creation. It enabled you to create layered maps using your data as well as Google Maps data.

name: Songza
description: Songza was a free music streaming service that would recommend its users' various playlists based on time of day and mood or activity.

name: Google Code
description: Google Code was a service that provided revision control, an issue tracker, and a wiki for code documentation.

name: iAd
description: Apple's mobile advertising platform. Steve Jobs said it would "reinvent" mobile advertising. It never seriously challenged Google, and Apple shut the network down after six quiet years.

name: iPhone Headphone Jack
description: The 3.5mm audio port was present on every iPhone for 9 years. Apple called its removal "courageous" in 2016 and included a Lightning adapter in the box. The box no longer ships.

name: QuickTime for Windows
description: Apple's media player for Windows, kept alive for over 20 years. Killed in 2016 with critical security vulnerabilities still unpatched. Users were advised to uninstall immediately.

name: Thunderbolt Display
description: Apple's last standalone external monitor before the Pro Display XDR. Discontinued in 2016 without a direct Apple replacement, leaving pro Mac users waiting until 2019.

name: WebObjects
description: A powerful web application server born at NeXT that Apple used to run the iTunes Store. Quietly deprecated in 2016 with no migration path for the enterprise customers who relied on it.

name: Game Center app
description: Apple's standalone iOS app for achievements, leaderboards, and multiplayer matchmaking. The service survived, but the app was removed in iOS 10 after years of neglect.

name: Apple TV (3rd gen)
description: The streaming set-top box that never got an App Store. It played video and little else, and lingered as the cheaper Apple TV until Apple finally discontinued it in 2016.

name: iTunes Radio
description: Apple's free ad-supported streaming radio service, built into iTunes and iOS. A direct Pandora rival, folded into Apple Music within three years without so much as a goodbye.

name: Apple Watch (Series 0)
description: The original Apple Watch, launched in 2015 amid breathless hype as the future of wearables. Sluggish and short on battery, it was retroactively nicknamed 'Series 0' once Series 1 arrived.

name: FireWire
description: Apple's high-speed serial bus for digital video and audio professionals. Faster than USB at launch, eventually beaten by cheaper USB and Thunderbolt, and gone from the last Mac with built-in FireWire by 2016.

name: MagSafe (laptop)
description: The magnetic power connector that detached harmlessly when someone tripped over the cable, saving countless MacBooks from broken ports. Removed in 2016 for USB-C, then restored on MacBook Pro five years later.

name: MacBook Air (11-inch)
description: The tiny wedge-shaped MacBook Air that felt like a netbook from a better universe. Loved by travelers, students, and writers, then axed as Apple pushed larger Retina notebooks.

name: Apple Watch Edition (gold)
description: The original luxury Apple Watch made from 18-karat gold and sold for five-figure prices. Apple quietly retreated from the jewelry-store strategy and replaced it with ceramic.

name: Google Blog Search API
description: Google Blog Search API was a way to search blogs utilizing Google.

name: Google Earth Browser Plug-in
description: Google Earth Browser Plug-in allowed developers to embed Google Earth into web pages and included a JavaScript API for custom 3D drawing and interaction.

name: Timeful
description: Timeful was an iOS to-do list and calendar application, developed to reinvent the way that people manage their most precious resource of time.

name: Microsoft Forefront
description: Microsoft Forefront was a family of line-of-business security software designed to help protect computer networks, network servers and individual devices, which underlying technology was acquired from Sybari in 2005.

name: Picasa
description: Picasa was an image organizer and image viewer for organizing and editing digital photos.

name: Google Flu Trends
description: Google Flu Trends was a service attempting to make accurate predictions about flu activity.

name: Google Catalogs
description: Google Catalogs was a shopping application that delivered the virtual catalogs of large retailers to users.

name: Google Moderator
description: Google Moderator was a service that used crowdsourcing to rank user-submitted questions, suggestions, and ideas.

name: Android @ Home
description: Android @ Home allowed a user’s device to discover, connect, and communicate with devices and appliances in the home.

name: Windows Media Center
description: Windows Media Center was a digital video recorder and media player for Windows.

name: Google Helpouts
description: Google Helpouts was an online collaboration service where users could share their expertise through live video.

name: Microsoft Forefront Threat Management Gateway
description: Microsoft Forefront Threat Management Gateway (Forefront TMG), formerly known as Microsoft Internet Security and Acceleration Server (ISA Server), and Microsoft Proxy Server, was a network router, firewall, antivirus program, VPN server and web cache for Windows Server.

name: YouTube for PS Vita
description: YouTube for PlayStation Vita was a native YouTube browsing and viewing application for the PS Vita and PSTV game consoles.

name: BebaPay
description: BebaPay was a form of electronic ticketing platform in Nairobi, Kenya that was developed by Google in partnership with Equity Bank.

name: Google Play Edition
description: Google Play Edition devices were a series of Android smartphones and tablets sold by Google.

name: Google Glass Explorer Edition
description: Google Glass Explorer Edition was a wearable computer with an optical head-mounted display and camera that allows the wearer to interact with various applications and the Internet via natural language voice commands.

name: Word Lens
description: Word Lens translated text in real time on images by using the viewfinder of a device's camera without the need of an internet connection; The technology was rolled into Google Translate.

name: Apple Wireless Keyboard
description: Apple's long-running Bluetooth desktop keyboard line, from the chunky white full-size model to the slim aluminum version that shipped with iMacs for years. It finally lost its name when Apple rebooted the accessory lineup as Magic Keyboard.

name: Aperture
description: Apple's professional photo management and RAW editing suite, and Lightroom's closest rival for years. Killed in favor of Photos, which launched without many of Aperture's pro features.

name: Beats Music
description: Dr. Dre and Jimmy Iovine's streaming service, praised for human-curated playlists. Apple acquired Beats for $3 billion and shut Beats Music down the next year as Apple Music took over.

name: iPhoto
description: The photo management app bundled with every Mac for over 13 years. Replaced by Photos, a simpler, more iCloud-centric app that lost many of iPhoto's organizing features.

name: Newsstand
description: A dedicated iOS app folder for digital magazine and newspaper subscriptions. Publishers barely supported it; readers rarely opened it. Removed in iOS 9 and absorbed into Apple News.

name: iPhone 5c
description: The plastic, candy-colored iPhone marketed as the affordable option, sold alongside the premium 5s. It was outsold by the 5s in nearly every market and ended Apple's brief experiment with a mid-tier consumer iPhone.

name: HopStop
description: A transit directions app covering hundreds of cities before Apple Maps had serious public transport features. Apple bought it, used the knowledge, then shut it down as Maps gained transit directions.

name: Microsoft MapPoint
description: Microsoft MapPoint was a program and a service created by Microsoft that allows users to view, edit and integrate maps.

name: Acompli
description: Acompli was a mobile app that allowed for user interaction with email messages, calendars and cloud files of multiple accounts in one app launched in April 2014 and then acquired by Microsoft in December 2014.

name: Sidewinder
description: SideWinder was the name given to a family of digital game controllers for PCs consisting of joysticks, driving wheels, game controllers, and voice chat devices.

name: Orkut
description: Orkut was a social network designed to help users meet new and old friends and maintain existing relationships.

name: Microsoft Streets & Trips
description: Microsoft Streets & Trips (Microsoft AutoRoute) was a mapping program targeting the average consumer to do a variety of map related tasks in the North American region, such as route planning.

name: Microsoft Academic Search
description: Microsoft Academic Search was a research project and an academic search engine.

name: Games for Windows – Live
description: Games for Windows – Live (GFWL) was an online gaming service used by Games for Windows–branded PC titles that enables Windows PCs to connect to Microsoft's Live service.

name: Age of Empires Online
description: Age of Empires Online was a multiplayer online real-time strategy game developed by Robot Entertainment and Gas Powered Games and based upon the gameplay of the Age of Empires series.

name: Google TV
description: Google TV was a smart TV platform that integrated Android and Chrome to create an interactive television overlay.

name: Quickoffice
description: Quickoffice was a productivity suite for mobile devices which allowed the viewing, creating and editing of documents, presentations and spreadsheets.

name: Google Questions and Answers
description: Google Questions and Answers was a free knowledge market that allowed users to collaboratively find answers to their questions.

name: Wildfire Interactive
description: Wildfire by Google was a social marketing application that enabled businesses to create, optimize and measure their presence on social networks.

name: BufferBox
description: BufferBox was a Canadian startup that provided consumers 24/7 convenience of picking up their online purchases.

name: SlickLogin
description: SlickLogin was an Israeli start-up company which developed sound-based password alternatives, was acquired by Google and hasn't released anything since.

name: Google Schemer
description: Google Schemer was a Google service for sharing and discovering things to do.

name: Google Chrome Frame
description: Google Chrome Frame was a plugin for Internet Explorer that allowed web pages to be displayed using WebKit and the V8 JavaScript engine.

name: Google Notifier
description: Google Notifier alerted users to new emails on their Gmail account.

name: Bump!
description: Bump! was an iOS and Android mobile app that enabled smartphone users to transfer contact information, photos, and files between devices.

name: Google Offers
description: Google Offers was a service offering discounts and coupons. Initially, it was a deal of the day website similar to Groupon.

name: PixelSense
description: PixelSense (formerly called Microsoft Surface) was an interactive surface computing platform that allows one or more people to interact with a tabletop screen.

name: iPod classic
description: The hard-drive click-wheel iPod that defined the line for more than a decade. Discontinued in 2014 as Apple moved its music focus to flash storage, iPhone, and streaming.

name: Windows Home Server
description: Windows Home Server was intended to be a solution for homes with multiple connected PCs to offer file sharing, automated backups, print server, and remote access.

name: Zune Marketplace
description: Zune Marketplace was an online store that offered music, podcasts, TV shows, movies, music videos, and mobile applications.

name: Google Currents
description: Google Currents was a social magazine app by Google, which was replaced by Google Play Newsstand.

name: Google Checkout
description: Google Checkout was an online payment processing service that aimed to simplify the process of paying for online purchases.

name: Google Trader
description: Google Trader was a classifieds service run by Google in Ghana, Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria to help customers trade goods and services online.

name: iGoogle
description: iGoogle was a customizable Ajax-based start page or personal web portal.

name: SideShow
description: Windows SideShow (codenamed Auxiliary Display) was a feature introduced in Windows Vista to supply information such as e-mail, instant messages, and RSS feeds from a personal computer to a local or remote peripheral device or display.

name: MSN TV
description: MSN TV (formerly WebTV by WebTV Networks, Inc.) was a web access product consisting of a thin client device which used a television for display and the online service that supported it.

name: Microsoft TechNet
description: Microsoft TechNet was a Microsoft web portal and web service for IT professionals, containing documentation for Microsoft products, discussion forums, an evaluation center for downloading trialware, blogs for Microsoft employees and much more.

name: Google Latitude
description: Google Latitude was a location-aware feature of Google Maps, a successor to an earlier SMS-based service Dodgeball.

name: Google Reader
description: Google Reader was an RSS/Atom feed aggregator.

name: Nexus Q
description: Nexus Q was a digital media player that allowed users with Android devices to stream content from supported services to a connected television or speakers via an integrated amplifier.

name: Punchd
description: Punchd was a digital loyalty card app and service targeted towards small businesses that originated as a student project at Cal Poly in 2009 and was acquired by Google in 2011.

name: Building Maker
description: Building Maker enabled users to create 3D models of buildings for Google Earth on the browser.

name: Google Talk
description: Often remembered as 'Gchat', Google Talk was a messaging service for both text and voice using XMPP.

name: Google SMS
description: Google SMS let you text questions- including weather, sports scores, word definitions, and more- to 466453 and get an answer back.

name: Google Cloud Connect
description: Google Cloud Connect was a free cloud computing plugin for multiple versions of Microsoft Office that automatically stored and synchronized files to Google Docs.

name: Picnik
description: Picnik was an online photo editing service that allowed users to edit, style, crop, and resize images.

name: Microsoft Office Picture Manager
description: Microsoft Office Picture Manager (formerly Microsoft Picture Library) was a raster graphics editor included up to Office 2010 to organize and edit images.

name: MSN Messenger
description: MSN Messenger (later rebranded as Windows Live Messenger) was a cross-platform instant messaging client.

name: Windows Live Mesh
description: Windows Live Mesh (formerly known as Windows Live FolderShare, Live Mesh, and Windows Live Sync) was a file synchronization application supporting both direct PC-to-PC and cloud-based synchronization and featuring Remote Desktop capability through the browser.

name: Microsoft XNA
description: Microsoft XNA was a freeware set of tools with a managed runtime environment provided by Microsoft that facilitates video game development and management, based on the .NET Framework, with versions that run on Windows NT, Windows Phone and the Xbox 360.

name: Microsoft Office PerformancePoint Server
description: Microsoft Office PerformancePoint Server was a business intelligence software product and it was generally an integration of the acquisitions from ProClarity, quickly merged in SharePoint Server 2010.

name: Cards
description: An iOS app for designing physical letterpress greeting cards that Apple would print and mail for you. Charming, oddly tactile, and dead less than two years later.

name: Google Chart API
description: Google Chart API was an interactive Web service that created graphical charts from user-supplied data.

name: Google Mini
description: Google Mini was a smaller version of the Google Search Appliance.

name: Microsoft Expression Studio
description: Microsoft Expression Studio was a suite of tools for designing and building Web and Windows client applications and rich digital media content.

name: AdSense for Feeds
description: AdSense for Feeds was an RSS-based service for AdSense that allowed publishers to advertise on their RSS Feeds.

name: Google Listen
description: Google Listen was an Android application that let you search, subscribe, download, and stream podcasts and web audio.

name: Google Refine
description: Google Refine was a standalone desktop application for data cleanup and transformation to other formats.

name: Zune (software)
description: Zune (software) was a media management software that functions as a full media player application with a library, an interface to the Zune Marketplace, and as a media streaming server.

name: Sparrow
description: Sparrow was an email client for OS X and iOS. Google acquired and then killed it.

name: Google Insights for Search
description: Google Insights for Search was a service used to provide data about terms people searched in Google and was merged into Google Trends.

name: Postini
description: Postini was an e-mail, Web security, and archiving service that filtered e-mail spam and malware (before it was delivered to a client's mail server), e-mail archiving.

name: Google Video
description: Google Video was a free video hosting service from Google, similar to YouTube, that allowed video clips to be hosted on Google servers and embedded onto other websites.

name: Microsoft Reader
description: Microsoft Reader was an application for reading e-books, specialized for .lit format.

name: Meebo
description: Meebo was a browser-based instant messaging application which supported multiple IM services.

name: ProClarity
description: ProClarity was a desktop business intelligence software suite that enabled the user to understand information contained within large volumes of organization data, which took the name from the homonymous company.

name: Google Commerce Search
description: Google Commerce Search was an enterprise search service that powered online retail stores and e-commerce websites that improved speed and accuracy.

name: Needlebase
description: Needlebase was a point-and-click tool for extracting, sorting and visualizing data from across pages around the web.

name: Zune
description: Zune was a line of digital media products and services.

name: Microsoft Hohm
description: Microsoft Hohm was an web application that enables consumers to better understand their energy usage and provided money saving recommendations.

name: Windows Live
description: Windows Live was a brand-name for a set of web services and software products from Microsoft as part of its software-as-a-service platform.

name: Knol
description: Knol was a Google project that aimed to include user-written articles on a range of topics.

name: Google Wave
description: Google Wave was an online communication and collaborative real-time editor tool.

name: Google Flu Vaccine Finder
description: Google Flu Vaccine Finder was a maps mash-up that showed nearby vaccination places across the United States.

name: Google One Pass
description: Google One Pass was an online store developed by Google for media publishers looking to sell subscriptions to their content.

name: Google Related
description: Google Related was introduced to be an experimental navigation assistant launched to help people find useful and interesting information while surfing the web.

name: Urchin
